fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. David says, "There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines." I think he figures Saul, who has been searching for him, won't follow him there. Running to the Philistines is a bold move, because the Philistines are gathering to fight Israel later in this very passage.

Michal the daughter of Saul is a name that might come to mind, friend, but this verse doesn't list her. It names his two wives as Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel. Michal isn't among them here. The second wife is Abigail, the widow of Nabal.

That's right, baker. The text says that when Saul learned David had fled to Gath, "…he no longer searched for him." Remember, David had said that if he escaped, Saul would stop searching all over Israel. Well, it worked out just like he said.
The text says the opposite, friend. When Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, "…he no longer searched for him." So the search stopped. David's plan to slip out of Saul's hand worked.

Careful here, baker. The text says David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. But when Achish asked, David said, "The Negev of Judah…" or "The Negev of Jerahmeel…" or "The Negev of the Kenites." Those names are different from the peoples the text says he raided. He gave Achish a whole menu of answers.

That's right, baker. The text says David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. But when Achish asked, David answered, "The Negev of Judah…" or "The Negev of Jerahmeel…" or "The Negev of the Kenites." Those names are different from the peoples the text says he raided.

Staying home would've been quieter, friend, but that's not what Achish says. He tells David, "You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me." So the order is for David and his men to go out to the fight. Guarding Gath isn't part of it.

That's the word, baker. David says, "Then you will come to know what your servant can do." Achish answers, "Very well… I will make you my bodyguard for life." A bodyguard stands right next to the king, so that's a big job to hand somebody.
Commander has a nice ring, friend, like a title you'd put on a mug. But Achish says, "I will make you my bodyguard for life." That's what he says he will do for David. So the word is bodyguard.
